messages.author: e42733d45d835f4a
messages.subject: Legend Label Issue
parts:
Ladies and Gentleman,

I am attempting to create a time series line chart, and I have almost everything created and working. The code is below:

ggplot (SAT, aes(Year))+
  geom_line(aes(y= Verbal, linetype = "Verbal"))+
  geom_line(aes(y= Math, linetype ="Math")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2003) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(510,530,by=1), "Score") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000,2010,by=1), "Year")

The only problem is that I can't get the legend label to change. Right now the title of the legend is "Verbal", but I would like to change it to "Score" unfortunately anything I do just messes up the rest of the code.
 
I have tried adding:

scale_linetype_manual("Score", (1,2)) but that gives me an "Error: unexpected ',' in "  scale_linetype_manual("Score", (1,"

also:

scale_linetype_manual("Score", c("Verbal" = "Solid", "Math" = "Dashed")) but that returns "Error in grid.Call.graphics("L_lines", x$x, x$y, index, x$arrow) : invalid line type: must be length 2, 4, 6 or 8"

I think the issue here is that I am not really understanding the difference between setting and mapping and this is screwing up my use of scale_linetype_manual, but I am not sure.

Any suggestions on how to fix this would be much appreciated...

Thanks,
Dmitry

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Legend Label Issue
parts:
Hi,

I can't reproduce your example without data, but these lines are
probably incorrect,

geom_line(aes(y= Verbal, linetype = "Verbal"))+
geom_line(aes(y= Math, linetype ="Math")) +

you'll want all aesthetics without quotes to perform the mapping,

geom_line(aes(y= Verbal, linetype = Verbal))+
geom_line(aes(y= Math, linetype = Math)) +


(or else, use aes_string)

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Legend Label Issue
parts:
On Sat, Nov 20, 2010 at 8:18 AM, Dmitry Berman <rave...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dennis,

Thanks that got it, and yes "section" is a better label. But, why did it get it? I'm not sure of what I just did to there, be totally honest....

Dmitry

When you use the manual scale, it is expected that you want to change more than the legend title - typically, one either wants to change the group labels, colors, shapes, linetypes, etc. I've just kind of learned through experience that if all you want to do is change the legend title, it's easiest to avoid manual scales. There are others who can probably explain the technical reasons better than I.

Even better would have been to plan ahead. Knowing that you wanted different linetypes for different sections, you could have melted the data to create a factor variable whose levels are the variable names Verbal and Math and whose values are stacked in the constructed variable 'value'. This little trick was one of the reasons the function was developed in the first place. Now you can map the variable names to linetype, have the names you want in the legend labels and the title you want by resetting the variable names in the melted data frame passed in the ggplot() call. Observe:

library(reshape2)
dm <- melt(d, id = 'Year')
names(dm) <- c('Year', 'Section', 'Score')
g <- ggplot(dm, aes(x = Year, y= Score))
g + geom_line(aes(linetype = Section)) + ...

No scale adjustment is necessary now and no need to rename the x and y labels (although you may want to still play with the axis ticks).

HTH,
Dennis
